threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You find out the hard way that no one uses the actual bus stops; it’s all about waving down the drivers on the road.
Last night on the 35, heard two blokes debating which chicken shop is the real ‘best’ in Brixton. They nearly got kicked off for rowdiness!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was home when I saw a guy juggling with his dog on a skateboard outside the kebab shop at 3 AM last weekend. Only in Neukölln.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you catch a live DJ set in a laundromat while folding your clothes. It's like a party where your socks are the guests.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know a native when they pass a mural and still stop to admire the untouched bits of paint; tourists just snap photos without a glance at the history.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a whole street perform a synchronized sigh when the driver announced another 'technical delay' at Civic Center. Classic Muni.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think bars close at midnight here. In Gràcia, it’s common to find locals chatting over vermut until dawn, especially during summer.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they’re still using Google Maps to navigate La Vila, while locals effortlessly shortcut through the alleys.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You start calling the Overground the 'Orange Line' without knowing it’s actually a train, not a Tube.
Caught a night bus last week and saw a guy playing an accordion while a couple argued over whose turn it was to pay for takeout. Classic Brixton.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was really living in Neukölln when I saw a street performer juggling flaming torches while a group of kids on scooters cheered him on.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find techno parties in abandoned warehouses alongside sausage stands selling currywurst at 4 AM. It's a wild mix of old and new.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s local when they can name all the taco spots that still have their old-school menus, not just the trendy ones.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo waiting for the 6 at 3 AM. He got on, looked around, and said, 'Well, at least someone's dressed for the occasion.'

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the nightlife, but the real charm is in the quiet morning chatter at the bakery on Carrer Verdi.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their reluctance to sit on the benches in Plaça del Sol. They haven’t yet embraced the art of people-watching.
